finding.claim: Attacker-supplied callbackUrl is stored at subscribe time with no validation and later used as the target of a server-side POST by the scheduled notifyAll job, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl) at src/Jobs.java:13 (documented as POST /subscribe body at line 12; route handler not in repo)
finding.sink: client.send(req, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()) at src/Jobs.java:24, with URI from URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) accepts the URL with no checks
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores the attacker-controlled URL
notifyAll iterates over all stored callback values (runs every minute)
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored value
client.send issues a POST to the attacker-chosen URL; response body is discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: None at subscribe time or send time: no scheme, host, IP-range, port, or allowlist checks. Mitigating factors: java.net.http.HttpClient only supports http/https so file: and other schemes are unreachable; HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER (client at src/Jobs.java:10) so redirects cannot move requests to other hosts; response body is not returned to the attacker, so the SSRF is blind; POST body is server-chosen (payload parameter of notifyAll), not attacker-controlled.

verdict.guard_found: none. No validation on callbackUrl at src/Jobs.java:13-14, and none at send time in notifyAll (lines 19-24). The only URL check, the regex at src/Jobs.java:30, is in thumb() and is not on this path. The HttpClient at line 10 uses default redirect handling, which the candidate correctly notes.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (src/Jobs.java:13, 14, 19, 21, 24), and nothing in the repo validates the stored URL. Whether an unauthenticated attacker reaches callbackUrl depends on the POST /subscribe handler (src/Jobs.java:12), which is not in the repo, so exposure cannot be decided here; if that route is reachable without auth, the finding would be CONFIRMED.
